name: Ithream
overview: Ithream was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known as the sixth-born son of King David. His identity is primarily grounded in his royal lineage as a son of the prominent Israelite king. There are no additional notes or details recorded about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Ithream means 'remainder of the people.' This proper name, as recorded in 2 Samuel 3:5, is not indicated to have been given directly by God. It reflects a Hebrew origin and carries a meaning that may signify a remnant or portion of the people.
familyAndRelationships: Ithream was the son of King David and his wife Eglah, as explicitly stated in Scripture. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ithream's significance lies in his position within the royal family of David, highlighting the lineage and offspring of Israel's anointed king. As the sixth-born son, he represents part of the broader family dynamics and succession context of David's reign. His mention in 2 Samuel 3:5 situates him within the historical and theological narrative of God's covenant with David and the establishment of his dynasty.
